name: libarchive native C library
verification_scope: Primary documentation and source-manifest review; no package execution, interoperability test, or OPFS implementation in this research.
evidence_level: Documented capability; integration assessments and caller policies are proposals, not executed results.
catalog_mapping_note: Existing IDs identify related catalog concepts; they do not claim that this implementation is an existing OPFS dependency or driver.
lifecycle: Current upstream release observed; format and codec support still depend on build configuration.
read_support: Multi-format reader, including tar/PAX/cpio, ZIP/ZIPX, 7z, RAR4/5, ISO, CAB, WARC and XAR. RAR support has documented limitations.
write_support: Creates tar/PAX/cpio, ZIP/ZIPX, 7z, ISO, WARC, XAR and other listed formats. RAR creation is not listed. No general in-place archive update API.
encryption_read: ZIP password decryption is verified by upstream AES tests; encrypted 7z/RAR support is not established by the reviewed documents.
encryption_write: ZIP AES writer options are exercised by upstream tests and require a cryptographic build dependency. Do not infer encryption for every writable format.
encrypted_listing: The upstream ZIP AES test lists names and sizes before a password is supplied; payload encryption does not imply hidden metadata.
runtime_unknown: Browser, Deno, Node and Bun require a separately assessed native binding or WASM build.
access_model: Callback-driven, predominantly sequential processing. The project explicitly does not promise general random member access or in-place changes.
streaming_and_staging: Can process data without loading a whole archive. A format-specific seek callback or restart may still be necessary; a replacement archive needs its own destination.
byte_limits: The streaming architecture is not a whole-archive memory limit. Entry and codec limits remain format- and build-specific.
metadata: archive_entry and disk APIs can preserve ownership, permissions, times, links, ACLs, flags and xattrs where the format and destination support them.
abort_and_cleanup: Integration must stop callbacks and close/free archive handles on every exit. Disk extraction finalizes some directory metadata on close.
extraction_safety: Disk API has explicit secure-symlink, no-dotdot and no-absolute-path flags; the cited manual says these checks are not the default. Enforce output budgets separately.
atomic_output: ARCHIVE_EXTRACT_SAFE_WRITES stages and renames individual extracted files. It does not make a complete multi-file extraction transactional.
license: New BSD license stated by upstream; enabled dependencies require their own review.
opfs_assessment: Candidate native bridge or separately pinned WASM backend. Prefer entry-byte callbacks over giving an extractor unrestricted destination paths.

name: 7-Zip native CLI and libraries
verification_scope: Primary documentation and source-manifest review; no package execution, interoperability test, or OPFS implementation in this research.
evidence_level: Documented capability; integration assessments and caller policies are proposals, not executed results.
catalog_mapping_note: Existing IDs identify related catalog concepts; they do not claim that this implementation is an existing OPFS dependency or driver.
version_observed: Official homepage and downloads list 26.05, released 2026-10-21.
lifecycle: Current native release observed; this version must not be attributed to older WASM ports.
read_support: Unpacks its writable formats and a larger read-only set including RAR, CAB, ISO/UDF, disk images and several filesystem images.
write_support: Official list: 7z, XZ, BZIP2, GZIP, TAR, ZIP and WIM. Read support for a format does not imply creation support.
encryption_read: The official feature list establishes AES-256 support for 7z and ZIP. Additional password formats/methods need separate verification.
encryption_write: Officially documents AES-256 for 7z and ZIP. Pinned 7z writer source has a separate he property for header encryption.
encrypted_listing: 7z header encryption is separate from payload encryption. WinZip AES leaves names visible; PKWARE central-directory encryption is a different profile outside this claim.
runtime_unknown: No native browser API; Deno/Node/Bun would invoke a process or a separately assessed binding.
access_model: Member selection is a CLI operation, not proof of cheap byte-range access. Solid compression can couple extraction of multiple members.
streaming_and_staging: Memory use depends on codec dictionary and solid-block choices. An OPFS process integration needs controlled local staging and output collection.
byte_limits: The published 7z format size ceiling is not a practical process, filesystem or WASM allocation guarantee.
metadata: Unicode names and format-specific metadata; preservation differs by archive format and operating system.
abort_and_cleanup: OPFS integration must own the subprocess, exit status, cancellation and temporary-output cleanup. No JavaScript AbortSignal contract is claimed.
extraction_safety: Candidate adapter must validate member paths/types and extraction quotas and confine native output to a staging directory.
atomic_output: Do not equate a successful individual write with atomic publication of the entire extraction or replacement archive.
license: Upstream states LGPL for most code, BSD-3-Clause for some parts, and unRAR restrictions for some components.
opfs_assessment: Native multi-format route. A new driver would map listing/extraction/creation separately and reject unsupported combinations.

name: libzip native ZIP library
verification_scope: Primary documentation and source-manifest review; no package execution, interoperability test, or OPFS implementation in this research.
evidence_level: Documented capability; integration assessments and caller policies are proposals, not executed results.
catalog_mapping_note: Existing IDs identify related catalog concepts; they do not claim that this implementation is an existing OPFS dependency or driver.
version_observed: Official reference documentation identifies current version 1.12.1.
lifecycle: Current upstream documentation observed; selected compression and crypto backends remain build choices.
read_support: ZIP reading, member lookup, metadata and encrypted-member reads.
write_support: Create and modify ZIP archives, including add/replace/delete and explicit commit/discard.
encryption_read: Encrypted ZIP member APIs and per-method capability query are documented.
encryption_write: WinZip AES-128/192/256 and traditional PKWare encryption are documented. The manual warns that traditional PKWare encryption is insecure.
encrypted_listing: These per-member encryption methods do not establish encrypted central-directory support.
runtime_unknown: Browser/WASM and JavaScript runtime bindings were not validated.
access_model: Opening an archive from a custom source requires seek/tell support. zip_fseek within a member is documented only for stored, unencrypted data.
streaming_and_staging: New member data can come from streamed read sources. A writable archive source must implement begin, commit, rollback and seek-write semantics.
byte_limits: API offsets and sizes use explicit 64-bit integer types; a JavaScript bridge must retain exact integer and buffer limits.
metadata: Archive/member attributes, timestamps, names and extra fields have dedicated APIs.
abort_and_cleanup: zip_close commits and frees only on success. On error the handle remains owned by the caller; zip_discard frees without saving. A registered cancel callback interrupts zip_close.
extraction_safety: It exposes member data; destination confinement, name collisions, link policy and decompression limits remain adapter responsibilities.
atomic_output: File-backed close can fail on temporary-file creation or rename. Custom sources must provide real commit/rollback rather than destructively overwriting their original.
opfs_assessment: A native custom-source bridge can map seekable reads and staged replacement. This is not automatically a browser-ready dependency.

name: zip.js
verification_scope: Primary documentation and source-manifest review; no package execution, interoperability test, or OPFS implementation in this research.
evidence_level: Documented capability; integration assessments and caller policies are proposals, not executed results.
catalog_mapping_note: Existing IDs identify related catalog concepts; they do not claim that this implementation is an existing OPFS dependency or driver.
version_observed: Reviewed master package manifest says 2.24.0; online API documentation reviewed on 2026-11-05. Package execution and release equivalence were not tested.
lifecycle: Current project documentation with explicit multi-runtime compatibility; pin the adopted release and its worker/WASM assets.
read_support: ZIP/ZIP64 and split ZIP, STORE/DEFLATE and documented DEFLATE64 decoding; metadata enumeration and streamed member extraction.
write_support: ZIP/ZIP64 creation, streamed entry output, parallel compression and split-output options; changing an existing archive normally creates replacement output.
encryption_read: WinZip AES and PKWare ZipCrypto are documented. AES authentication checking defaults to true in the reviewed API.
encryption_write: Password/raw-password options, AES strength and ZipCrypto selection are exposed.
encrypted_listing: Do not treat per-entry AES/ZipCrypto as hidden filenames or claim support for PKWARE encrypted central directories without a separate fixture.
runtimes: Browsers: Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge (publisher compatibility table)
runtime_unknown: Exact minimum versions differ by native-JavaScript, WASM and core build; this research did not execute them.
access_model: ZipReader reads the central directory first. A plain ReadableStream is buffered fully; custom Reader.readUint8Array(index,length), lazy Blob or HttpRangeReader avoids that whole-input buffering.
streaming_and_staging: Parallel entry compression automatically enables buffering. createTempStream can put each temporary compressed entry on OPFS or another store; its dispose hook runs after success, error or abort.
byte_limits: ZIP64 support does not remove runtime Number, typed-array, quota or codec limits. Apply explicit member-count and actual-output budgets.
metadata: Writer options expose timestamps, comments, extra attributes, Unix mode/uid/gid and DOS attributes. A portable filesystem cannot necessarily apply them all.
abort_and_cleanup: Entry read/write options accept AbortSignal; ZipReader.close and async disposal are documented, and terminateWorkers ends the shared worker pool. Own temporary-stream disposal separately.
extraction_safety: Reviewed options include structural ambiguity/overlap checks. CRC32 checking defaults to false, AES authentication to true. These checks do not replace path/type/size policies.
atomic_output: The writer targets a sink; a filesystem adapter must stage and commit the final archive or extracted file after validation.
license: BSD-3-Clause in the reviewed package manifest.
opfs_assessment: Direct typed range-reader and stream-writer seam; the existing OPFS helpers are evidence that temporary storage is a distinct lifecycle, not permission to assume whole-archive random writes.

name: fflate
verification_scope: Primary documentation and source-manifest review; no package execution, interoperability test, or OPFS implementation in this research.
evidence_level: Documented capability; integration assessments and caller policies are proposals, not executed results.
catalog_mapping_note: Existing IDs identify related catalog concepts; they do not claim that this implementation is an existing OPFS dependency or driver.
lifecycle: Current project documentation reviewed; an upstream ZIP64 allocation issue was reported for 0.8.3 and was not reproduced here.
read_support: ZIP STORE/DEFLATE plus gzip, zlib and raw DEFLATE; complete-buffer and streaming unzip APIs.
write_support: ZIP creation and gzip/zlib/DEFLATE compression, synchronous, callback-based and streaming forms.
encryption_read: No password-decryption API verified; do not advertise encrypted ZIP support.
encrypted_listing: Encrypted archive support is outside the verified contract.
runtime_unknown: Bun was not explicitly established by the reviewed evidence.
access_model: Buffer-based ZIP operations or sequential streaming Unzip; no range-reader provider contract established.
streaming_and_staging: Async streams expose queuedSize/ondrain; worker transfer can consume input buffers. Whole-result helpers still allocate complete results.
byte_limits: ZIP64 reading exists, but the changelog does not promise arbitrary-large entry support. Test sentinel-size handling and bound allocation before trusting metadata.
metadata: ZIP extra fields, comments and timestamps are available; not a native metadata restoration layer.
abort_and_cleanup: Async one-shot calls return a termination function; async streams and streamed entries expose terminate. A terminated one-shot callback is not invoked.
extraction_safety: The caller chooses output paths and limits. A parser returning a filename is not an extraction sandbox.
atomic_output: Caller owns destination staging and commit.
license: No license conclusion required for this capability assessment; verify the selected package license before embedding.
opfs_assessment: Codec/streaming ZIP route with explicit backpressure and cancellation adaptation; no broad encrypted/large-ZIP claim.

name: JSZip
verification_scope: Primary documentation and source-manifest review; no package execution, interoperability test, or OPFS implementation in this research.
evidence_level: Documented capability; integration assessments and caller policies are proposals, not executed results.
catalog_mapping_note: Existing IDs identify related catalog concepts; they do not claim that this implementation is an existing OPFS dependency or driver.
lifecycle: Current documentation reviewed; browser support examples include historical runtimes and are not a current benchmark.
read_support: Classic ZIP, data descriptors and limited ZIP64 loading. STORE and DEFLATE.
write_support: Create/edit the logical file set and generate a new ZIP; streamFiles uses data descriptors.
encryption_write: Encrypted ZIP support is not part of the documented feature set.
encrypted_listing: Password-protected input is rejected rather than providing a guaranteed metadata-only view.
runtime_unknown: Deno and Bun were not independently verified.
access_model: loadAsync accepts complete byte/string/Blob input and merges entries by name; no native remote-range reader is documented.
streaming_and_staging: async/generateAsync hold the complete result. Node streams or StreamHelper permit chunk consumption; streamFiles alone does not remove whole-result accumulation.
byte_limits: The limitations page says ZIP64 values must fit its 32-bit processing assumptions; do not equate ZIP64 parsing with practical >4GiB support.
metadata: Round-tripping may discard metadata and add folders; native encoding support is UTF-8 with caller-provided decoders for other names.
abort_and_cleanup: StreamHelper offers pause/resume. A general AbortSignal cancellation/cleanup contract is not established by these docs.
extraction_safety: loadAsync strips relative .. components since 3.8.0 and retains unsafeOriginalName; duplicate names overwrite in its object model. CRC verification is opt-in.
atomic_output: Caller must publish a successfully generated or validated result through a separate staged write.
license: MIT or GPLv3 dual license, stated by upstream.
opfs_assessment: Convenience ZIP manipulation route with explicit size and memory scope, not an encrypted or range-native archive driver.

name: Web CompressionStream / DecompressionStream
verification_scope: Primary documentation and source-manifest review; no package execution, interoperability test, or OPFS implementation in this research.
evidence_level: Documented capability; integration assessments and caller policies are proposals, not executed results.
catalog_mapping_note: Existing IDs identify related catalog concepts; they do not claim that this implementation is an existing OPFS dependency or driver.
version_observed: WHATWG Living Standard last updated 2026-10-19 in the retrieved page.
lifecycle: Web standard implemented by runtimes; algorithm availability must be probed in the deployed runtime.
read_support: Streaming decompression of the standard gzip, deflate (zlib framing) and deflate-raw formats; no archive-member parser.
write_support: Streaming compression of those formats; no ZIP/tar directory, entry metadata, append or update API.
encrypted_listing: Not applicable: it has no archive listing.
runtime_unknown: Runtime-specific extra algorithms and exact version support are not portable standard guarantees.
access_model: Forward stream transform. No random decompressed-byte access without a separate seekable format/index.
streaming_and_staging: Uses readable/writable Web Streams; accumulating a final Blob or ArrayBuffer is a caller choice, not a streaming guarantee.
byte_limits: No application-level decompressed-byte budget is supplied by the standard. Count produced bytes and propagate cancellation.
metadata: Only compression framing; no filesystem metadata contract.
abort_and_cleanup: Use stream cancellation/abort and release locks through the enclosing pipeline; there is no separate archive handle.
extraction_safety: No path handling. A valid compressed stream can still expand beyond application resources.
atomic_output: Destination staging remains external to the transform.
license: Platform API; no bundled codec package is implied.
opfs_assessment: Reusable codec layer under tar or another container, or a transparent stream transform. Do not call it archive support.

read_support: UntarStream parses a tar byte stream into entries and member streams.
write_support: TarStream creates tar from typed file/directory/link inputs. File input requires path, size and readable content.
encryption_write: None in tar; compose a separate envelope if required.
encrypted_listing: An external whole-archive envelope would require decryption before this parser.
runtimes: Deno, explicitly indicated by the package

metadata: Typed input includes per-entry metadata options and entry kind. Destination metadata support must be assessed separately.
abort_and_cleanup: Use the Web Streams pipeline lifecycle and ensure open Deno files are closed on cancellation/error.
extraction_safety: The package example normalizes a path before writing; normalization alone is not destination confinement. Enforce path/link/collision/output-size rules in the adapter.
atomic_output: Caller supplies staged sinks and publication policy.
license: Package license was not independently inspected in this capability pass.
opfs_assessment: Native stream-shaped integration possibility for Deno; cross-runtime availability remains an explicit validation task.

name: node-unrar-js
verification_scope: Primary documentation and source-manifest review; no package execution, interoperability test, or OPFS implementation in this research.
evidence_level: Documented capability; integration assessments and caller policies are proposals, not executed results.
catalog_mapping_note: Existing IDs identify related catalog concepts; they do not claim that this implementation is an existing OPFS dependency or driver.

lifecycle: Wrapper and native core update status are separate; do not infer current UnRAR fixes from the wrapper name.
read_support: RAR listing/extraction from an ArrayBuffer or native file; the README explicitly excludes multi-volume archives.

extraction_safety: Avoid direct file extraction for untrusted names until filenameTransform, symlink and containment behavior are reviewed.
atomic_output: Caller staging required; extraction success and complete iteration are separate lifecycle requirements.
license: Wrapper manifest says MIT; the compiled UnRAR source is separately governed by RARLAB terms.
opfs_assessment: Read-only RAR route with a material early-exit cleanup constraint; not a full multi-volume/recovery engine.
